newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Motta sees "special position" for telcom nat'ls.
newsitem.headline: Motta sees "special position" for telcom nat'ls.

text.p: Brazilian Communications Minister Sergio Motta said national firms are likely to have a "special position" in the make-up of joint ventures to operate regional telecom firms.
"We're seeking to stimulate joint ventures where domestic capital will have a special position," Motta told reporters.
Motta did not specify what he meant by a "special position."
But he said a 49-percent limit on foreign participation in consortia forming to bid on Brazil's B Band cellular concessions in the coming months had not posed a problems in drawing foreign interest.
Brazilian law allows the executive to limit foreign participation on any telecoms service in Brazil and such restrictions on foreign capital are common around the world, Motta said.

But he stressed the importance of drawing foreign investors to take part in the privatization of Brazil's telecommuncations sector and added foreigners based in the country would not suffer any restrictions.
"We're going to allow total freedom to stimulate companies to be based here," Motta said.
"It is fundamental. There is not enough capital in Brazil to meet a problem of this size," he added, referring to Brazil's antiquated telecoms infrastucture.

Twenty consortia, many led by foreign companies, are expected to bid on concessions to operate cellular in the B Band and the world's largest telecoms operators are interested in Brazil's massive fixed-line and cellular market.
